summary: This note covers notable milestones from the knockout stage of the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia. It highlights Belgium's comeback from two or more goals down to win a knockout match within 90 minutes, the first such comeback since Portugal's 1966 quarter-final win over North Korea. It also notes Japan's six goals at the tournament, their highest World Cup total, and Belgium's first quarter-final appearances in successive World Cups.
one_line: Notable milestones from the 2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage, including Belgium's comeback win and Japan's six goals.
key_facts: Belgium became the first team to come from two or more goals down to win a World Cup knockout stage match within 90 minutes since Portugal beat North Korea in the 1966 quarter-final.
Portugal beat North Korea 5-3 in the 1966 quarter-final after being 3-0 down.
Belgium's comeback was the first from two goals down in a World Cup knockout match since West Germany's 3-2 victory over England in 1970.
West Germany's 1970 comeback over England ended 3-2.
Japan scored six goals at Russia 2018, their highest ever tally in a single World Cup tournament.
Belgium reached the World Cup quarter-finals in successive tournaments for the first time.
